title: CAMA Paper Complete Draft
summary: Complete NeurIPS 2025 paper draft for Cardinality-Aware Moment Aggregation (CAMA), a lightweight drop-in module that enriches mean aggregation at FK joins in relational deep learning with gated per-dimension variance injection. All sections written in full prose with LaTeX math notation. Experimental results marked as PLACEHOLDER pending experimental validation. Includes 5 figure specifications, 3 table specifications, 18-reference bibliography with verified citations, and claim-to-evidence mapping distinguishing established theoretical claims from pending empirical ones.
answer:
The complete CAMA NeurIPS 2025 paper draft contains all sections: Abstract (152 words), Introduction (~1200 words), Related Work (~720 words), Method (~1000 words), Experiments (~2000 words), Discussion and Limitations (~580 words), Conclusion (~180 words), totaling approximately 5830 words of content text (excluding references and appendix outline). The paper is structured around the central thesis that mean aggregation at FK joins in relational deep learning compresses distributional information, and CAMA addresses this via gated variance injection conditioned on log-cardinality [1, 2, 3].

Key technical contributions verified through web research:

1. NOVELTY CONFIRMED: No prior work combines per-dimension variance as informative signal (not normalization) with cardinality-gated injection specific to FK joins [4]. The closest methods are PNA (uniform multi-aggregation, no gating) [5], GNN-VPA (variance normalization, not enrichment) [6], and GenAgg (globally learned f-mean, no per-node adaptation) [7].

2. THEORETICAL ANCHOR VERIFIED: Xu et al. (ICLR 2019) Lemma 5 proves sum aggregation can represent injective functions over multisets of bounded size, while mean and max cannot [8]. This is correctly cited as motivation for why mean aggregation loses information.

3. RELBENCH TASKS VERIFIED: All proposed experimental tasks confirmed as real RelBench tasks with correct metrics [9, 10]: rel-amazon (user-churn AUROC, user-ltv MAE, item-churn AUROC), rel-f1 (driver-dnf AUROC, driver-position MAE), rel-stack (user-engagement AUROC, post-votes MAE), rel-hm (user-churn AUROC, item-sales MAE), rel-avito (user-visits AUROC, ad-ctr MAE).

4. TERMINOLOGY VALIDATED: 'Information compression' is correctly distinguished from 'rank collapse' [11]. Roth & Liebig's rank collapse is depth-wise across layers; CAMA targets within-step compression at single FK aggregation. Nait Saada et al.'s width-wise collapse in attention [12] is the closest conceptual relative but uses a different remedy (rank-one subtraction) not applicable to FK joins.

5. CITATION DETAILS VERIFIED for all 18 references [1-18]: correct authors, venues, years, and arXiv IDs confirmed through web search and page fetches.

6. NEURIPS 2025 FORMAT CONFIRMED: 9 content pages + unlimited appendix, LaTeX required [13].

7. GRIFFIN AUTHOR CORRECTION: The dependency listed 'Pelevin' but actual authors are Wang, Wang, Gan, Wang, Yang, Wipf, Zhang [14]. Corrected in the draft.

8. SCOPE HONESTY maintained throughout: every section acknowledges CAMA targets mean-aggregation architectures only; sum and attention-based methods already preserve distributional information.

figures.description: Information compression at FK join: N child embeddings in embedding space compressed via mean aggregation into single centroid (left) vs. CAMA enriched parent preserving distributional information via gated variance injection (right). Two contrasting cases: (a) homogeneous children where gate closes, (b) diverse children where gate opens.

CAMA module architecture diagram. Left: standard mean aggregation at FK join (N children -> message transform -> 1/N sum -> mu). Right: CAMA (same children -> mean mu AND per-dimension variance sigma^2 -> cardinality gate g=sigmoid(w*logN+b) -> enriched output m = mu + g * W_sigma * sigma^2). Annotate gate behavior at high vs low N.

Information compression severity across edge types and databases. X-axis: edge types sorted by median cardinality. Y-axis: compression ratio (intra-group variance / total variance). Color-coded by database. Expected pattern: higher cardinality = greater compression.
Per-task Cohen's d with 95% CI for CAMA vs Mean. One row per task, horizontal CI bars. Classification (blue) vs regression (red). Diamond at bottom for pooled effect. Vertical dotted line at d=0.

Learned gate values by FK edge type (rows, sorted by median cardinality) x task (columns). Color scale 0 (blue, closed) to 1 (red, open). Expected patterns: gates open more for high-cardinality edges and classification tasks.

tables.description: Main results: 11 tasks x 4 methods (Mean/Sum/PNA/CAMA) with delta column. Tasks across rel-amazon, rel-f1, rel-stack, rel-hm, rel-avito. Metrics: AUROC (classification), MAE (regression). Last row: pooled Cohen's d.
Ablation study on selected task. Rows: Mean, Mean+Var(ungated), Mean+Gate(no var), CAMA(full), Sum, PNA. Columns: metric value, delta vs mean, p-value.
RelGNN integration as scope validation (expected negative result). RelGNN vs RelGNN+CAMA on 3 tasks. Purpose: confirm CAMA unnecessary for attention-based architectures.

claim_evidence_map.claim: Mean aggregation is not injective over multisets; sum is
RelBench uses sum aggregation by default, overriding SAGEConv's mean
PNA applies all aggregators uniformly with no gating
VPA normalizes variance for stability, does not enrich features
Roth & Liebig rank collapse is depth-wise across layers, not within-step
Width-wise rank collapse exists in attention but remedy differs from CAMA
No prior work combines gated variance injection with cardinality conditioning at FK joins
claim_evidence_map.source: Web search 2026-03-19: no matching papers found

claim_evidence_map.claim: GenAgg uses globally shared parameters without per-node adaptation
RelGNN improves routing but retains standard aggregation
Griffin uses mean intra-relation aggregation susceptible to information compression
CAMA improves over mean aggregation on RelBench tasks
Gate learns meaningful behavior (opens at high-cardinality diverse joins)
No catastrophic failure on any task (safe default property)
CAMA does not help RelGNN (scope validation)
Information compression severity correlates with CAMA improvement
Classification tasks benefit more than regression tasks
Ungated variance injection helps but gating improves further

terminology_constraints: Use 'information compression' NOT 'rank collapse' when describing CAMA's target phenomenon
Use 'CAMA' (Cardinality-Aware Moment Aggregation) throughout, NEVER 'RAMA' or 'AMA'
Use 'distributional information' or 'diversity profile' to describe what mean loses
Use 'enriches' for CAMA (additive information), 'normalizes' for VPA (variance control)
Never claim CAMA is 'state-of-the-art'; use 'bridges the gap between mean and sum'

key_design_decisions.base_architecture: HeteroSAGE with MEAN aggregation (not RelBench default sum)
key_design_decisions.base_architecture_rationale: Test on the architecture CAMA is designed to improve. Sum as baseline shows what CAMA approaches.
key_design_decisions.gate_formulation: g = sigmoid(w * log(N) + b), scalar per edge type
key_design_decisions.gate_rationale: Log-cardinality is the distinguishing FK-join property, cheaply available. Simpler than effective-rank variant.
key_design_decisions.variance_projection: W_sigma in R^{d x d} per edge type

sources.title: RelBench: A Benchmark for Deep Learning on Relational Databases (Robinson et al., NeurIPS 2024)
sources.summary: Primary benchmark paper. Confirmed 11 databases, 30+ tasks, sum aggregation as default overriding SAGEConv mean. Authors: Robinson, Ranjan, Hu, Huang, Han, Dobles, Fey, Lenssen, Yuan, Zhang, He, Leskovec.

sources.title: How Powerful are Graph Neural Networks? (Xu et al., ICLR 2019)
sources.summary: Theoretical anchor. Lemma 5: sum can represent injective multiset functions. Mean/max cannot. Authors: Xu, Hu, Leskovec, Jegelka.

sources.title: Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs (Hamilton et al., NeurIPS 2017)
sources.summary: GraphSAGE paper. Mean aggregation default. Authors: Hamilton, Ying, Leskovec.

sources.title: GNN-VPA: A Variance-Preserving Aggregation Strategy (Schneckenreiter et al., ICLR 2024)
sources.summary: Variance-preserving (1/sqrt(N)) normalization for training stability. Distinct from CAMA's enrichment approach. Authors: Schneckenreiter, Freinschlag, Sestak, Brandstetter, Klambauer, Mayr.

sources.title: Principal Neighbourhood Aggregation for Graph Nets (Corso et al., NeurIPS 2020)
sources.summary: PNA: 4 aggregators x 3 degree scalers = 12 operations, applied uniformly. Authors: Corso, Cavalleri, Beaini, Lio, Velickovic.

sources.title: RelGNN: Composite Message Passing for Relational Deep Learning (Chen et al., ICML 2025)
sources.summary: SOTA on RelBench via atomic routes and attention aggregation. Improves routing, not aggregation quality. Authors: Chen, Kanatsoulis, Leskovec.

sources.title: Griffin: Towards a Graph-Centric Relational Database Foundation Model (Wang et al., ICML 2025)
sources.summary: Foundation model using mean intra-relation + max inter-relation aggregation. Authors: Wang, Wang, Gan, Wang, Yang, Wipf, Zhang. NOTE: dependency listed 'Pelevin' as author but this is incorrect.

sources.title: Rank Collapse Causes Over-Smoothing and Over-Correlation in GNNs (Roth & Liebig, LoG 2024)
sources.summary: Depth-wise rank collapse theory. Proposition 5.6: amplification depends only on aggregation matrix. Authors: Roth, Liebig.

sources.title: Attention is Not All You Need: Pure Attention Loses Rank Doubly Exponentially (Dong et al., ICML 2021)
sources.summary: Depth-wise collapse in transformers. Skip connections and MLPs mitigate. Authors: Dong, Cordonnier, Loukas.

sources.title: Mind the Gap: Spectral Analysis of Rank Collapse in Attention Layers (Nait Saada et al., 2024)
sources.summary: Width-wise rank collapse in softmax attention as context grows. Stable rank collapses O(T^{-3}). Authors: Nait Saada, Naderi, Tanner.

sources.title: Generalised f-Mean Aggregation for GNNs (Kortvelesy et al., NeurIPS 2023)
sources.summary: Learned parametric f-mean aggregator. Globally shared, no per-node adaptation. Authors: Kortvelesy, Morad, Prorok.

sources.title: On the Bottleneck of GNNs and its Practical Implications (Alon & Yahav, ICLR 2021)
sources.summary: Over-squashing: exponential information compressed into fixed-size vectors. Distinct from information compression. Authors: Alon, Yahav.

sources.title: The Effective Rank: A Measure of Effective Dimensionality (Roy & Vetterli, EUSIPCO 2007)
sources.summary: Effective rank = exp(Shannon entropy of normalized singular values). Range [1, rank(A)]. Authors: Roy, Vetterli.

follow_up_questions: What hidden dimension and number of GNN layers should be used for fair comparison across all baselines, and should these match RelBench's default training configuration or be independently tuned?
Should the effective-rank gate extension (Appendix B) be included in the main experiments as an additional row, or kept strictly in the appendix to maintain focus on the simpler log-N gate?
How should the paper handle the case where CAMA's improvements on regression tasks are not statistically significant -- should these tasks be dropped from the main table or retained for transparency?
